title: Greater Manchester mayoral election polling stations open

input.summary: Polling stations are open across Greater Manchester as voters elect the region's next mayor
input.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election polling stations open - BBC News Image source, EPA Image caption, Polls have opened across Greater Manchester for the mayoral election By Georgie Docker North West Published 1 hour ago Polling stations across Greater Manchester have opened in a mayoral election that was triggered when Andy Burnham resigned as the city region's mayor. MPs are not permitted to be mayor, meaning Burnham had to stand down after his success in last month's Makerfield parliamentary by-election. His election as an MP paved the way for him becoming prime minister earlier this month. Voters are now choosing which candidate they would like to represent them as mayor of Greater Manchester and leader of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority. Polling stations opened at 07:00 BST and will close at 22:00. The results are due to be announced on Friday. Here is a list - in alphabetical order, by surname - of the seven candidates who are standing in the mayoral election: Sian Astley, Reform UK Geraldine Coggins, Green Party Bev Craig, Labour Phil Eckersley, Conservative Marcus Farmer, Independent Richard Kilpatrick, Liberal Democrats Marlon West, Restore Britain The election will be decided using the supplementary vote (SV) system - meaning voters can choose to select both a first- and second-choice candidate. If nobody wins more than 50% of the initial vote, all but the two highest-polling candidates are knocked out of the race. The second choices of those who voted for the other candidates are then reallocated. Whichever of the top two candidates ends up with the most votes after this "run-off" round is then declared the winner. input.lead: Avanti West Coast staff working at Manchester Piccadilly announce a 24-hour walk-out on Saturday
input.summary: Avanti West Coast staff working at Manchester Piccadilly announce a 24-hour walk-out on Saturday
input.evidence_text: Manchester PiccadillyRail strike planned over 'unfair sacking' - BBC News Image caption, The RMT says the sacked colleague was a "victim of a toxic workplace culture" By Ewan Gawne North West Published 29 July 2026 Staff working at Manchester's busiest rail station are set to strike on Saturday over what their union has said is the unfair sacking of a colleague. About 70 Avanti West Coast members who are part of the RMT and work at Manchester Piccadilly have announced plans for a 24-hour strike, with further walk-outs planned. The action comes after what the union said was the dismissal of a staff member based on "anonymous allegations" over which they have taken industrial action four times in the past two months. Avanti West Coast has been contacted for comment. RMT general secretary Eddie Dempsey said the sacked worker had "clearly been the victim of a toxic workplace culture which encouraged anonymous and unsubstantiated complaints". He claimed the worker had been "made a scapegoat for multiple management failings". The union wants to see the dismissal overturned, with further strikes scheduled for 29 August and 10 October. title: Man badly injured climbing between double Metrolink tram in Manchester

input.lead: Police said the man had potentially life-changing injuries after the incident at Market Street in Manchester
input.summary: Police said the man had potentially life-changing injuries after the incident at Market Street in Manchester
input.evidence_text: Man badly injured climbing between double Metrolink tram in Manchester - BBC News Image source, Geograph/Chadwick Image caption, A large cordon was in place around Market Street By Ewan Gawne North West Published 29 July 2026 A man has suffered potentially life-changing injuries after getting trapped climbing into the space between a double tram in Manchester city centre. The incident happened at the Market Street Metrolink tram stop at about 09:20 BST, Greater Manchester Police said. The man, aged in his 50s, was taken to hospital for treatment. A cordon was placed around the busy city centre station, close to the city's Arndale Centre shopping complex, while police carried out investigations. Transport for Greater Manchester said: "Staff supported emergency services while the stop was cordoned off and the scene has now been cleared. "Service changes remain in place across Metrolink and customers are advised to check the latest travel advice before making journeys by tram." The incident meant tram services on the Bury Line were terminating at Manchester Victoria only. Trams on the Ashton Line were ending at Piccadilly, while there was no service between Piccadilly and Victoria. title: Baby found 'emaciated' 19 days after social services closed case

input.lead: The girl was covered in sores, severely dehydrated and had "paper-thin skin" when she was treated
input.summary: The girl was covered in sores, severely dehydrated and had "paper-thin skin" when she was treated
input.evidence_text: Baby found 'emaciated' 19 days after social services closed case - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, The 19-month-old girl was less than half the weight a child should be on average for her age By Jonny Humphries North West Published 29 July 2026 An "incredibly emaciated" and starving baby, covered in sores, was taken to hospital in a critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, a review has found. The 19-month-old girl weighed 9.7lb (4.4kg) - less than half the 24lb (11kg) expected for an average child of her age - when she was treated in February 2025. A Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, reported the girl was severely dehydrated, had no fatty tissue noted on her body and had "paper-thin skin". The case was closed despite warnings her mother, who was 17 when the baby was born, was neglecting her daughter and had avoided social workers and health visitors for weeks. Rochdale Borough's Safeguarding Children Partnership said it accepted the findings of the review and was "taking action". The CSPR, which referred to the girl as Child K1, said she displayed "skin breakdown" across the "entirety" of her bottom and nappy area. Expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall said medics found "wasting to the buttocks" and open pressure sores extending along her back, hips and bottom. She wrote: "Child K1's presentation of hypothermia, hypoglycaemia [low blood sugar], severe malnutrition, dehydration along with renal failure, evidenced by severe abnormality of blood salts, could have led to death if it had not been identified and emergency treatment initiated." input.evidence_text: Manchester tower block that would have dwarfed city pub scrapped - BBC News Image source, Arrowsmith Management Image caption, Plans to build a tower block next to the Britons Protection pub have been withdrawn By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 29 July 2026 A plan to build a 26-storey block of flats next to one of Manchester's most famous pubs has been scrapped. The 72-apartment block was due to be built next to the Britons Protection on Great Bridgewater Street in the city centre. While a "sensitive approach" had been promised since the plans were first revealed in 2021, the previous and current landlords of the Grade II-listed pub opposed the move, arguing it would deprive the beer garden of all its sunlight. The developer, Arrowsmith Management, has been approached for comment. Established in 1806, the pub's name is said to be derived from the building's use as an army recruitment centre in the early part of the Napoleonic wars. It was recorded as having provided shelter to people fleeing the 1819 Peterloo Massacre in nearby St Peter's Field, where a yeomanry cavalry charge killed 18 protesters who were demanding broader voting rights. The hanging sign outside the pub shows military men on horseback trampling demonstrators who are carrying placards demanding reform. Image source, Google Image caption, The Britons Protection is more than 200 years old While there are tower blocks close to the pub, the Arrowsmith plan would have seen a block built directly next to it. When the plans were submitted in 2021, the pub's landlord at the time, Mark West, said he feared it could have spelled the end for the pub, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said . Ashley Crowder will learn his fate next week having been convicted of the murder of Graham Cox last month A sentencing hearing at Bolton Crown Court began on Wednesday (July 29) and is due to continue on August 6. Crowder, 37, held Mr Cox, 37, hostage at his Farnworth flat for two weeks and drained his bank account in 2024 Paramedics who found popular DJ and father Mr Cox said he was 'cold to the touch' and that there were signs of 'rigor mortis'. His body was found under a blanket on a sofa, jurors were told Mr Cox reported that he had gone 14 days without food, jurors at Crowder's trial heard. input.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. input.evidence_text: ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Павел Дедищев выступит в Лондоне со своим стендап концертом "АМЕРИКАНЕЦ" Лондон! 30го сентября к нам приезжает Павел Дедищев со своим концертом "Американец" Резидент шоу Stand Up на ТНТ, финалист «Comedy Баттл» и «Большого шоу», участник проектов «Решалы» и «Было слово». Он стоял у истоков объединения HIT2SHIT (будущего Labelcom), стал сооснователем канала «Комьюнити» и одним из тех, кто формировал новую волну русскоязычного стендапа. input.evidence_text: Rudy’s Pizza Napoletana has confirmed it will be bringing its relaxed dining experience and renowned Neapolitan pizzas to Salford for the first time, with a new restaurant opening in Monton village this autumn. To celebrate, the pizzeria is giving away 3,000 pizzas on the house a The new pizzeria, located at 237-239 Monton Road , will transform the former Bennetts Furnishers store that has been vacant since 2022, with work now officially underway. The spacious venue will mark Rudy’s 41st restaurant to date Since launching in Manchester’s Ancoats in 2015, Rudy’s has grown into one of the UK’s most loved pizzerias, celebrated for its light, double fermented dough and unwavering dedication to true Neopolitan craft Testament to its authenticity, Rudy’s is the largest organisation in the world to be accredited by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana (AVPN), the international body that protects and promotes traditional Neapolitan pizza making Rudy’s has also been recognised among the World’s 50 Best Pizzeria, ranking 23rd globally for 2025. Each pizza, from the classic Margherita to the fiery Calabrese, is made to AVPN standards using traditional techniques and ingredients sourced directly from Italy To claim one of 3,000 complimentary pizzas, Monton locals can sign up via this link , where they will be able to choose from Rudy’s favourites such as its Cinghiale , Margherita Con Bufala, and Triple Pepperoni to enjoy at the new opening this summer
